summary_note: Each row covers 240 bars (15 samples × 16 bars). MOSS is the server's synthesis time per request: two bars for v0.0 to v0.2, one bar for v1.0. Round trip is how long the Mac waited for a request, network included; in v1.0 a fetch is a long poll that can start before the bar's audio exists. Network is the median of five health checks over the SSH tunnel before each run. Timings are shown for real-time runs only, because fake real-time stops the clock while the server works.
method: Server: one NVIDIA H200 running Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on vLLM, MOSS-TTS v1.5 and the MMS aligner, with the same weights, reference voice and drums for every version. Client: an Apple Silicon Mac, connected to the H200 through an SSH tunnel.

Each version is its tagged commit, Mac client and server alike: rap-v0.0 (0a493cb8), rap-v0.1 (9b76415e), rap-v0.2 (0ea74a7f) and rap-v1.0 (19526512). All four read the same 15 scenario files (one topic and one flow template for 16 bars at 90 BPM) with the same seed per sample.

v0.0 and v0.1 run their servers with the all_onsets_r3 warp policy. Their default, gentle_sparse_r3, is rejected by their own Mac client (fixed in v0.2), which would turn every real-time bar into eSpeak. v0.2 and v1.0 warp on the Mac with their default policy.
The v0.0 and v0.1 Mac clients run on Python 3.12, installed from their own lock files, because the SciPy wheel locked for their pinned Python 3.10 no longer loads on this macOS. No code was changed.

Fake real-time runs the same code with a virtual clock that stops while the server works, and gives v0.0 to v0.2 requests a 60 s server budget. Nothing falls back for time there; the few fallbacks left come from the system itself: no valid lyric candidate on the server (v0.0 4 bars, v0.1 4, v0.2 6) or a response that failed the Mac's alignment check (v0.0 6 bars, v0.1 2).

Real-time fallbacks by cause. v0.0: 178 of 182 bars were late, because in-process MOSS takes about 2.8 s per two-bar request and a request takes about 4.7 s in total, against 5.3 s of music per chunk; a late request also blocks the next one, which then fails at once. v0.1: 12 late bars, 4 bars where the server failed to render, 2 bars that failed the Mac's check. v0.2: 12 late bars (three late chunks, each followed by one blocked chunk) and 6 bars with no valid lyric candidate. v1.0: none.

v0.0 and v1.0 were recorded alternately, sample by sample; v0.1 and then v0.2 were recorded after them, each on its own, because the GPU held only two server stacks at a time. Every batch started with an unrecorded warm-up run. One v0.1 fake real-time take (S10) was recorded again after a tunnel interruption cut one request off.

With the same seed, the fake real-time and real-time lyrics still differ, because the lyrics are sampled per run and a fallback line becomes context for later lines. The three older versions often end a line with a spoken "A", copied from their prompt; v1.0 fixed this.
Audio is each client's own recording (48 kHz, vocal plus drums), loudness-normalized to −16 LUFS and encoded as 192 kbps MP3.
